children.text: A fishing village at the southeastern tip of Cebu Island, where you can see whale sharks up close and swim with them in the waters off Tan-awan almost every day. After a dawn viewing, pairing it with Tumalog Falls, Sumilon Island, and a Spanish-era church makes for a full, rewarding day.
Oslob is a coastal town about
120km
south of Cebu City, at the southeastern tip of Cebu Island. Since around

, whale sharks fed shrimp by fishermen off the coast of Barangay Tan-awan have appeared almost daily, and the area has become known as one of the world's most reliable places to see whale sharks. Called 'butanding' in the local language, the whale shark is the world's largest fish, but a gentle animal that feeds on plankton and small shrimp; the individuals appearing off Oslob are usually juveniles about
long.

The viewing process is simple. From dawn until around noon, you register and receive a safety briefing at the beach briefing center, then take a small bangka just a few dozen meters offshore. As fishermen scatter krill from a small boat, the whale sharks rise close to the surface and open their mouths wide to feed, and snorkelers float beside the boat for about
30 minutes
, watching this right in front of them. There are also options to observe only from the boat, or to look up from below via scuba diving.

However, Oslob's whale shark tourism has been a subject of ongoing environmental controversy because of the feeding. Critics say feeding alters the whale sharks' natural migration behavior and causes injuries from boat collisions, while others point positively to a fishing village that once hunted whale sharks now making a living from protecting them and from tourism. Knowing about this controversy before visiting, and strictly following the rules, is the mark of a responsible traveler.
Oslob has more to see beyond the whale sharks. Tumalog Falls,
10 minutes

away by car, has an impressive curtain-like flow of water, the nearby Sumilon Island has a white sandbar, and the town center still has a 19th-century coral-stone church and the ruins of a Spanish barracks. A dawn-departure day tour from Cebu City or Mactan is the most common way to visit.
Administratively, Oslob is a small municipality of about 135 km² with 21 barangays and a population of about 29,000 (
census). The town center and Tan-awan, the whale shark viewing site, are about
10km
apart, so you need to travel separately to see the church and the Cuartel. The town began in
as a visita of Boljoon and became an independent parish in

, and a coral-stone watchtower built in the late 18th century to watch for pirates still stands on the coast. A lot of whale shark research has also accumulated: according to the Large Marine Vertebrates Research Institute (LAMAVE) in the Philippines, more than 400 individuals have passed through Oslob, of which 9 are resident individuals that stay year-round. More than 300 kg of shrimp feed is put in the water each day and most individuals bear scars, which is the basis of the environmental controversy.
Float beside the bangka and observe the whale sharks for about
30 minutes
. On many days several appear at once, so you can experience their enormous bodies passing right beside you.

If you hold a diving certification, you can watch the whale sharks from a few meters below the surface, looking up at them. There are fewer people than with snorkeling, and you can see their whole body, making for great photos.

A waterfall where thin streams of water cascade like a curtain down a moss-covered cliff. It's good for rinsing off and swimming after your whale shark viewing, and you ride a habal-habal down from the entrance to the falls.
Sumilon Island, off the coast of Oslob, was the Philippines' first marine protected area, famous for the white sandbar that appears at low tide. It's commonly included in Oslob day tours.
The Immaculate Conception Church, built of coral stone in the 19th century (restored after a fire in
), and the adjacent unfinished Spanish barracks ruin known as the Cuartel are photo spots with the sea as a backdrop.
Ruins of coastal watchtowers once used to watch for pirates in the Spanish era remain scattered along Oslob's shore. Take them in on a walk around the church.
From Liloan Port south of Oslob, a ferry crosses to Negros Island (toward Dumaguete) in about
20–30 minutes
. It's a good route to link a Cebu and Dumaguete trip.
About
13km
north of Oslob town, on the way back to Cebu City, Boljoon Church (Patrocinio de Maria Shrine Church) is a fortress-style church that the Augustinian friar Ambrosio Otero began building in
. The coral-stone walls and gates were built between
, and the church was designated a National Historical Landmark in
and a National Cultural Treasure in
. The museum on the convent's ground floor displays religious objects and old records.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night (overnight in Oslob)
items.subtitle: For those who want a relaxed dawn viewing

children.text: Leave from Cebu City's South Bus Terminal by bus or chartered vehicle. At Carcar Market along the way you can try lechon and chicharon.
Look around Boljoon Church before reaching Oslob.
See the church and the Cuartel at Oslob Heritage Park, then enjoy the sea view around sunset.
Check in to accommodation near Tan-awan and turn in early.
Walk from your accommodation to the registration counter and see the whale sharks in the first group.
After breakfast, take a habal-habal to Tumalog Falls. The waterside is quiet at this hour.
Take a boat to the Sumilon Island sandbar from Bangcogon Pier. Check the boat timetable the day before.
Have lunch, then head back to Cebu City, or go to Liloan Port and cross over to Negros.

children.text: Head from your Dumaguete accommodation to Sibulan Port. It takes about
15–20 minutes
by car from the town center to Sibulan Port.
Take the ferry from Sibulan Port to Liloan Port. The crossing takes about
30 minutes
, and there is also a first boat at
From Liloan Port, take a bus or habal-habal to Tan-awan, then register and get a safety briefing.
Snorkel with whale sharks.
Swim and rest at Tumalog Falls.
Head to Oslob town to see the church and the Cuartel at Heritage Park, and have lunch.
Return to Liloan Port and cross to Sibulan on the
3 PM
or 6 PM ferry. Check the last boat time on the day.
Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and Philippines AirAsia operate direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport, with a flight time of about
1 hour 25–30 minutes
. One-way fares start from around
US$32
on the cheapest days but vary greatly by date and airline. From the airport to Oslob, a private vehicle costs about
one way.
Even if you arrive on a morning flight from Manila, by the time you reach Oslob the registration cutoff may be close. We recommend a plan that includes a night in Cebu City or Oslob.
Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) is the closest, and it takes about
3 hours 30 minutes–4 hours 30 minutes
by car from the airport to Oslob. Using Dumaguete Airport (DGT) in Negros instead can actually be closer: about
30 minutes
from Dumaguete town to Sibulan port, about
20–30 minutes
by ferry to Liloan port, then about
20 minutes
by car to Oslob.
From Cebu City's South Bus Terminal, take a Ceres bus 'Bato via Oslob' or a bus bound for Santander/Liloan, and ask to be dropped off at Tan-awan (the whale shark viewing site). The trip takes about
3 hours 30 minutes–4 hours
, and the air-conditioned bus fare is about
. Fares differ by source because of fuel surcharges and other factors, so check at the terminal. Take the first bus at dawn to arrive with plenty of time for the morning viewing.
The first bus to Oslob leaves around
3 AM
, with departures every
1–2 hours
until evening (every
30 minutes
according to some sources). The trip takes longer if there is traffic. Check the latest timetable at the terminal counter.
A day tour with pickup from your Cebu City or Mactan accommodation between
3 and 5 AM
is the most convenient. A joiner tour including the whale shark viewing fee, Tumalog Falls or Sumilon Island, and lunch costs about
per person, while chartering just a vehicle costs about
per car. From Moalboal it's about
2 hours–2 hours 30 minutes
by car.
If you're coming from Dumaguete, ferries run frequently from Sibulan Port to Liloan Port (Santander), with fares of about
. From Liloan Port to Tan-awan in Oslob it takes about
20–30 minutes
by bus or habal-habal.
On the Liloan–Sibulan route, operators such as Maayo Shipping run several times a day from
until around
. Fuel surcharges and terminal fees may be added to the base fare at the counter, so check the timetable and fares on the
official Maayo Shipping site
From the whale shark viewing site to Tumalog Falls takes about
10 minutes
by habal-habal (motorcycle taxi), at about
one way. If you agree on a round-trip price and ask the driver to wait, you won't have to look for a ride at the falls.
Oslob Heritage Park in the town center is about
9km
away; take a bus running between Cebu City and Santander, or use a habal-habal. Public transport is infrequent, so arrange your way back in advance.
Whale sharks can be observed almost year-round thanks to the feeding. Still, the period from around
March
to
June
, when the sea is calm and visibility good, is the most comfortable, and during the dry season from
December–May
there's less worry about rain. Since Oslob is on Cebu's east coast, waves rise on days with strong northeast monsoon (amihan) winds from
November–February
, and viewing may be suspended during typhoon season (mainly
August–November
On weekends and during Korean and Chinese holidays and the Easter and Christmas seasons, tourist numbers surge and waiting times grow long. Arriving on a weekday early morning (
6–7 AM
) gets you clear water and fewer crowds. Oslob's town fiesta is held around the Feast of the Immaculate Conception on
December 8
Oslob's coast faces east toward the Cebu Strait, so you can watch the sun rise out of the sea. According to local reports from
May 2026

, crowds run 800–900 people a day on weekdays and more than 1,000 on weekends, and can exceed 2,000 in peak season. If you're late in the registration order you'll wait a long time to get in the water, so arriving early is the surest approach.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions. The whale shark viewing fee was raised in
March 2025
, so check the latest fee notice.

Most people visit as a day trip, but if you want a relaxed dawn viewing, staying overnight in Oslob is a good option. Small resorts and guesthouses line the coastal road around the viewing site, running about
a night, with sea-view resorts around
. If you can walk to the viewing site from your accommodation, you can get in the water first without waiting at dawn.

The food scene is simple. Restaurants in front of the viewing site and along the coastal road sell Filipino-style seafood set meals like grilled fish, kinilaw, squid dishes, and chicken barbecue. At the town market you can easily find traditional Filipino rice cakes like biko and puto made from cassava and coconut, and buy cheap mangoes, a southern Cebu specialty, on the street.

Where to stay falls into three areas. Along the Tan-awan coast, small resorts and guesthouses cluster close to the viewing site, while Oslob town is close to Heritage Park and quiet. The only place you can stay on Sumilon Island itself is Bluewater Sumilon Island Resort, a 4-star property. On the way from Cebu City, the lechon and chicharon at Carcar Market and the torta of Argao (a sponge cake made with tuba) are famous foods.
Viewing usually runs from
until around noon, and registration may close around
. Arrive as early as possible.
You can't apply sunscreen before entering the water. Cover up from the sun with a rash guard and long swimwear instead.
To prevent your mask from fogging in the water, apply anti-fog solution beforehand or rinse the mask well.
Since all you need to do is get off the bangka and float, you can join with a life vest even if you can't swim.
For photos, use the on-site paid photography service or an action cam. Always turn off your flash.
The viewing fee is basically cash, so prepare change, and since foreigner and local rates differ, bring your passport.
Moving on from Oslob to Moalboal or Dumaguete lets you plan a loop through southern Cebu.
Tumalog Falls is quietest between
7–9 AM
. Whale shark tour groups usually start crowding in around
10 AM

Visit Oslob Heritage Park in the morning or around sunset, when it's not hot and the light is good for photos. Public transport to town is inconvenient, so arrange a round trip with a habal-habal driver.
Children face an age limit for entering the water. Many notices say children under 7–8 years old cannot enter the water, so check the on-site rules and have them watch from the boat.
Touching or riding a whale shark, or blocking its path, is prohibited, and you must keep a distance of at least about
4m
. Violations can result in a fine.
A whale shark's tail fin is extremely powerful. Don't get close to the tail.
Flash photography and sunscreen use are prohibited. If you break the rules, the guide may stop your session.
The long dawn journey can cause severe motion sickness and fatigue, so bring motion sickness medicine and snacks.
Touts around the viewing site sometimes push unofficial tours, so use the official registration counter.
Even with feeding, whale sharks do not always appear. For four days,

, no whale sharks showed up in the viewing area and the experience was suspended. Check with the local tourist office or your tour operator the day before whether it is operating, and if it is suspended, switch your plans to Sumilon Island or Tumalog Falls.
Oslob's whale shark viewing is an activity with environmental controversy over feeding. If you take part, strictly follow the rules on maintaining distance and no contact.
